findings.title: Redundant Redis memory info queries across per-process SpansBuffer instances
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, `buffer.get_memory_info()` is now called in a loop over `self.buffers.values()` (one `SpansBuffer` per flusher process) instead of once on the main `SpansBuffer`. If `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` queries the underlying Redis cluster hosts (rather than strictly the assigned shard keys) or if multiple shard subsets map to the same Redis nodes, iterating over every `shard_buffer` issues N times as many `INFO memory` calls to Redis on every batch submission and sums duplicate `ServiceMemory` entries. Using a single `SpansBuffer` (or deduplicating by host) avoids multiplying Redis round-trips by `num_processes`.

findings.title: `join()` fails to terminate remaining flusher processes when the timeout expires
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes` checks `if remaining_time <= 0: break` before reaching `process.terminate()`. When a `timeout` is provided and the first process (or `self.next_step.join(timeout)`) consumes the entire timeout budget, the loop breaks early and any subsequent flusher processes in `self.processes` are never terminated, leaving orphaned background processes running after `join()` returns. Instead of `break`, the loop should skip the `while process.is_alive()` wait and still call `process.terminate()` on all remaining alive processes.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key (`shards` vs `shard`) in `SpanFlusher.main`
findings.body: Lines 185 and 195 tag `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` with `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, whereas line 199 tags `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` with `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` (plural). Additionally, When a flusher process handles multiple shards, `shard_tag` is a comma-separated string like `"0,2"`, while `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` at line 244 emits individual integer shard tags. Using different tag keys (`shard` vs `shards`) and formats makes dashboarding and filtering across flusher metrics inconsistent.
